rulebook: N.J.A.C. 3A:52 Manual of Requirements for Child Care Centers (effective Dec. 20, 2023)

findings.requirement: Centers operating during normal waking hours may not care for a child on a regular basis for more than 12 hours within a 24-hour period.
findings.quote: Centers operating during the normal waking hours shall not care for a child on a regular basis for more than 12 hours within a 24-hour period
findings.handbook_quote: We are open Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

findings.requirement: Centers operating during normal sleeping hours may not care for a child on a regular basis for more than 16 hours within a 24-hour period.
findings.quote: Centers operating during the normal sleeping hours shall not care for a child on a regular basis for more than 16 hours within a 24-hour period

findings.requirement: The center must give every parent and staff member the Office of Licensing Information to Parents document and keep signed receipts.
findings.quote: The center shall give to the parent(s) of every enrolled child and to every staff member, a written Information to Parents document designated by the Office of Licensing
findings.handbook_quote: When you enroll, we give you the Office of Licensing's Information to Parents document and ask you to sign a form confirming you received it.

findings.requirement: The Information to Parents document must indicate how parents can secure a copy of the chapter and obtain licensing process information from the Office of Licensing.
findings.quote: Indicate how parents can secure a copy of this chapter and obtain information about the licensing process from the Office of Licensing
findings.handbook_quote: To get your own copy or to learn about the licensing process, contact the Office of Licensing, Department of Children and Families, PO Box 717, Trenton, NJ 08625-0717, toll-free 1-877-667-9845.

findings.requirement: Parents must receive advance notice of field trips, outings, or special events involving transportation, and written consent must be secured before taking a child.
findings.quote: Provide parents with advance notice of any field trip, outing or special event involving the transportation of children away from the center, and, for each event, secure the written consent of the parent(s) before taking a child on such a field trip, outing or special event
findings.handbook_quote: Your child goes only if you sign a permission slip for that trip.

findings.requirement: The Information to Parents document must state that parents may review and discuss questions or concerns about center policies or compliance with the director, sponsor, or sponsor representative.
findings.quote: Afford parents the opportunity and time to review and discuss with the center director, sponsor, or sponsor representative any questions or concerns about the policies and procedures of the center or whether the center is in compliance with all applicable provisions of this chapter
findings.handbook_quote: You are always welcome to set a time with our director, or with our owner, who serves as the center's sponsor representative, to review and discuss any question or concern about our policies and procedures or about whether we are following the state's licensing rules.

findings.requirement: The Information to Parents document must advise parents that suspected violations may be reported to the center sponsor, sponsor representative, director, or Office of Licensing.
findings.quote: Advise parents that if they believe or suspect that the center is violating any requirement of this chapter, they may report such alleged violations to the center sponsor, sponsor representative, or director or to the Office of Licensing
findings.handbook_quote: If you believe or suspect that we are violating any licensing requirement, you may report it to our director, our sponsor representative, or directly to the Office of Licensing at 1-877-667-9845.

findings.requirement: Staff must verbally notify the State Central Registry Hotline immediately when there is reasonable cause to believe a child has been abused or neglected.
findings.quote: The sponsor, sponsor representative, director, or any staff member shall verbally notify the State Central Registry Hotline (1-877 NJ ABUSE/1-877-652-2873) immediately whenever there is reasonable cause to believe that a child has been subjected to abuse or neglect
findings.handbook_quote: Any staff member who has reasonable cause to believe a child has been abused or neglected calls the State Central Registry Hotline at 1-877-NJ ABUSE (1-877-652-2873) immediately.

findings.requirement: Staff must advise parents the same day of unusual incidents that might indicate possible abuse or neglect involving the child.
findings.quote: the sponsor, sponsor representative, director, or any staff member shall advise the parent(s) of the occurrence of any unusual incident(s) that occurred at the center and that might indicate possible abuse or neglect involving the child. Such notification shall be made on the same day on which the incident occurred
findings.handbook_quote: If something unusual happens at the center that might suggest abuse or neglect involving your child, we will tell you the same day.

findings.requirement: CARI consent forms and related correspondence must be kept confidential.
findings.quote: the sponsor, sponsor representative, and all staff members shall keep all completed CARI consent forms and related correspondence confidential
findings.handbook_quote: Staff Child Abuse Record Information (CARI) forms and related letters are kept confidential.

findings.requirement: The center must conduct two lockdown drills per year and keep records.
findings.quote: The center shall conduct two lockdown drills per year and maintain on file a record of each lockdown drill
findings.handbook_quote: We also hold two lockdown drills each year.

findings.requirement: The center must conduct fire drills at least once a month and evacuate all children within three minutes.
findings.quote: The center shall conduct fire drills at least once a month, as specified in the NJUFC
findings.handbook_quote: We hold a fire drill every month, including one during nap time each year, and every child must be out of the building within three minutes.

findings.requirement: At least two staff members with current certified basic first aid and CPR knowledge must be in the center whenever enrolled children are present.
findings.quote: At least two staff members who have current certified basic knowledge of first aid principles and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), as defined by a recognized health organization (such as the American Red Cross), shall be in the center at all times when enrolled children are present
findings.handbook_quote: At least two staff members with current first aid and CPR certification are in the building whenever children are here.

findings.requirement: Centers must develop a written policy on television, computer, and video equipment use for children over two and maintain written plans for such use.
findings.quote: Centers shall develop a written policy regarding the use of television, computers, and other equipment for children over the age of two and maintain on file written plans for such use and the length of time for their use
findings.handbook_quote: Children under two never use televisions, computers, tablets, or other video equipment at Saltmeadow Sparrow.

findings.requirement: The center must prepare and maintain a written outline of its daily activities.
findings.quote: The staff member(s) specified in (b) above shall prepare and maintain on file a written outline of the center's daily activities
findings.handbook_quote: Our teachers prepare a written outline of each classroom's daily activities, which we keep on file and post outside each classroom.

findings.requirement: Food for children present during normal mealtimes or required snack periods must be provided by the parent or the center.
findings.quote: Food served to children who are present during normal mealtime hours or required snack periods, as specified in (b) and (c) below, shall be provided either by the child's parent or by the center
findings.handbook_quote: We serve breakfast, lunch, and an afternoon snack that meet federal Child and Adult Care Food Program standards.

findings.requirement: A snack must be served to all children in care at least three consecutive hours and all children served on an after-school basis.
findings.quote: A snack shall be served to all children who are under the center's care for at least three consecutive hours and for all children who are served on an after-school basis
findings.handbook_quote: Every child who is with us three or more hours in a row gets a snack, and drinking water is always available.

findings.requirement: Drinking water must be made available to all children.
findings.quote: Drinking water shall be made available to all children
findings.note: Beam marked this as covered, but the words it quoted don't appear in your handbook exactly as written (it may have joined two lines, such as two rows of a table).

findings.requirement: Staff may not force-feed or coerce a child to eat against the child's will.
findings.quote: Staff members shall not force-feed or coerce a child to eat against his or her will
findings.handbook_quote: Staff never force-feed a child or pressure a child to eat.

findings.requirement: For children under 18 months, the center must develop and follow a feeding plan with each child's parent.
findings.quote: The center shall develop mutually with each child's parent(s) and follow a feeding plan regarding the feeding schedule, specific formula, breastfeeding arrangements and accommodations
findings.handbook_quote: For children under 18 months, we work out a feeding plan with you covering the feeding schedule, formula or breast milk, breastfeeding arrangements, and new foods.

findings.requirement: Children 12 months or younger must initially be placed face-up for sleep unless a health care provider indicates otherwise in writing.
findings.quote: For children 12 months of age and younger, the center shall ensure that each child is initially placed in a face-up sleeping position unless a different position is indicated in writing by the child's health care provider
findings.handbook_quote: Babies 12 months and younger are always placed on their backs to sleep, unless your child's health care provider tells us in writing to use a different position.

findings.requirement: Swaddling children during rest and sleep is prohibited.
findings.quote: Swaddling of children during rest and sleep is prohibited
findings.handbook_quote: we never swaddle babies or other children during rest or sleep.

findings.requirement: The center must maintain and follow a written policy on releasing children and give it to parents and staff with signed receipts.
findings.quote: The center shall maintain on file and follow a written policy on the release of children
findings.handbook_quote: This section is our written release policy, and each parent and staff member signs to confirm receiving it.

findings.requirement: A child may be released only to the parent or a person authorized by the parent.
findings.quote: each child may be released only to the child's parent(s) or person(s) authorized by the parent(s)
findings.handbook_quote: We release your child only to you or to an adult you have authorized in writing, and new pickup adults must show photo ID.

findings.requirement: Sleeping equipment must meet recognized safety organization standards and cribs must meet CPSC standards.
findings.quote: All sleeping equipment shall meet the standards of a recognized safety organization (such as the Juvenile Products Manufacturers Association, the American Society for Testing and Materials, or the United States Consumer Product Safety Commission)
findings.handbook_quote: Each baby sleeps in a crib that meets federal safety standards, with no pillows, bumper pads, or soft bedding.
findings.explanation: The handbook mentions crib safety for babies but does not say all sleeping equipment meets recognized safety standards.
findings.fix: All of our sleeping equipment, including cribs, cots, mats, and playpens, meets the standards of a recognized safety organization, and every crib meets federal safety standards.

findings.requirement: Only one child may occupy a crib, playpen, cot, mat, or other approved sleeping equipment at a time.
findings.quote: During rest and sleep periods, only one child shall occupy a crib, playpen, cot, mat, or other Office of Licensing-approved sleeping equipment at one time
findings.handbook_quote: only one child uses a crib, cot, or mat at a time.

findings.requirement: The release policy must include written procedures for when a parent or authorized person fails to pick up a child at closing.
findings.quote: Written procedures to be followed by staff member(s) if the parent(s) or person(s) authorized by the parent(s), as specified in (a)1 above, fails to pick up a child at the time of the center's daily closing
findings.handbook_quote: If an hour or more has passed since closing, we still have not reached anyone who can come, and staff can no longer stay, we will call the State Central Registry Hotline at 1-877-652-2873 for help caring for your child until you or an authorized adult arrives.

findings.requirement: The release policy must include procedures when a pickup person appears impaired and the child would be at risk.
findings.quote: Written procedures to be followed by a staff member(s) if the parent(s) or person(s) authorized by the parent(s), as specified in (a)1 above, appear to be physically or emotionally impaired
findings.handbook_quote: If a parent or authorized adult arrives appearing physically or emotionally impaired, for example under the influence of alcohol or drugs, to the point that the director or a teacher believes your child would be at risk of harm, we will not release your child to that person.

findings.requirement: School-age children may not be released unsupervised except upon written instruction from the parent.
findings.quote: No child shall be released from the program unsupervised except upon written instruction from the child's parent

findings.requirement: Staff may not discipline children for failing to eat or sleep or for soiling themselves.
findings.quote: Staff members shall not discipline children for failing to eat or sleep or for soiling themselves
findings.handbook_quote: Children are never disciplined for not eating, not sleeping, or toileting accidents.

findings.requirement: Active play time may not be withheld as discipline unless the child presents a danger.
findings.quote: Staff shall not withhold active play time as a means of discipline unless the child's actions or behavior present a danger to themselves or others
findings.handbook_quote: Teachers never take away outdoor or active play time as a consequence, unless a child's behavior at that moment puts the child or others in danger.

findings.requirement: The center must maintain a written discipline policy, post it prominently, distribute it to staff, and keep signed receipts.
findings.quote: The center shall maintain on file a written policy on the disciplining of children by staff members
findings.handbook_quote: This section is our written discipline policy. It is posted in the front lobby, every staff member receives a copy and signs for it, and a copy is always available to you.

findings.requirement: Staff may not use hitting, shaking, or any other corporal punishment.
findings.quote: Staff members shall not use hitting, shaking or any other form of corporal punishment of children
findings.handbook_quote: Staff never hit, shake, or use any other physical punishment, and never use abusive language, ridicule, or harsh, humiliating, or frightening treatment.

findings.requirement: Staff may not use abusive language, ridicule, harsh, humiliating, or frightening treatment.
findings.quote: Staff members shall not use abusive language, ridicule, harsh, humiliating or frightening treatment or any other form of emotional punishment of children
findings.handbook_quote: never use abusive language, ridicule, or harsh, humiliating, or frightening treatment.

findings.requirement: Staff may not withhold food, emotional responses, stimulation, or opportunities for rest or sleep.
findings.quote: Staff members shall not withhold from children food, emotional responses, stimulation, or the opportunities for rest or sleep
findings.handbook_quote: We never withhold food, comfort, attention, or rest from a child.

findings.requirement: Before a field trip, the center must inform parents whether a school bus, other approved school vehicle, or private passenger vehicle will be used and who will drive.
findings.quote: The center shall inform parents whether a school bus, other approved school vehicle, or private passenger vehicle will be used, and whether the driver will be a staff member, a parent, or another person
findings.handbook_quote: Before any field trip, outing, or special event that takes children away from the center by vehicle, we give you written notice at least one week ahead telling you where we are going, whether we will ride a school bus, another approved school vehicle, or a private passenger vehicle, whether the driver is a staff member, a parent, or someone else, and the name and phone number of any bus company.

findings.requirement: Parents may visit the center at any time during operating hours to observe without prior approval.
findings.quote: The center shall allow the parent(s) of enrolled children to visit the center at any time during the center's hours of operation to observe its operation and program activities without requiring the parent(s) to secure prior approval
findings.handbook_quote: You may visit the center at any time while we are open to watch your child's classroom and our program, with no need to call ahead or get permission.

findings.requirement: Early childhood programs must provide an enrollment conference covering operations, child needs, release, toilet training, medication, communicable disease policy, Information to Parents, and expulsion policy.
findings.quote: The center shall provide for the parents of each newly-enrolled child an opportunity to attend an enrollment conference
findings.handbook_quote: Before your child's first day, we invite you to an enrollment conference with the director. We go over our days and hours, talk about your child's habits, diet, sleep, behavior, and development, and review our policies on releasing children, toilet training, and giving medication.

findings.requirement: The center must develop and follow a written expulsion policy and give it to parents with signed receipts.
findings.quote: The center shall develop and follow a written policy on the expulsion of children from enrollment at the center
findings.handbook_quote: You will sign to confirm that you received this policy.

findings.requirement: A child may not be expelled solely because a parent complained to the Office of Licensing or questioned center policies.
findings.quote: The center shall not expel a child based solely on the child’s parent making a complaint to the Office of Licensing regarding a center’s alleged violations
findings.handbook_quote: We will never expel a child because a parent complained to the Office of Licensing or questioned our policies.

findings.requirement: The center must develop and follow a written social media policy and give it to parents and staff with signed receipts.
findings.quote: The center shall develop and follow a written policy on the use of social media
findings.handbook_quote: Every parent and staff member receives a copy of this social media policy and signs to confirm receiving it.

findings.requirement: In the event of temporary or permanent closure, the center must provide advance notice to parents in sufficient time to make alternative arrangements.
findings.quote: In the event of temporary or permanent closure of the center, the center shall provide advance notice to parents of enrolled children in sufficient time to enable parents to make alternative child care arrangements
findings.handbook_quote: If we ever plan to close temporarily or permanently, we will give you at least 30 days' notice so you have time to arrange other care.

findings.requirement: A well-child center may not admit a child with specified illnesses or symptoms unless a health care provider indicates in writing the child poses no serious health risk.
findings.quote: A center serving well children shall not permit a child who has any of the illnesses or symptoms of illness specified in (c)1i through xiii below to be admitted to the center on a given day unless medical diagnosis from a health care provider
findings.handbook_quote: A child may not attend with any of these symptoms unless a health care provider tells us in writing, or by phone with a written follow-up, that the child poses no serious health risk.

findings.requirement: If an admitted child shows specified illness symptoms, the center must remove the child from the well group to a separate area until taken home or cleared by a health care provider.
findings.quote: If a child who has already been admitted to the center manifests any of the illnesses or symptoms of illness specified in (c)1 above, the center shall remove the child from the group of well children to a separate room or area
findings.handbook_quote: If your child develops one of these symptoms here, we move your child to a separate, supervised area until you arrive or until the director speaks with a health care provider who says your child poses no serious risk.

findings.requirement: Early childhood programs must maintain each child's health examination, immunization record, and special care plan if applicable.
findings.quote: upon admission, the center shall maintain on file at the center a Universal Child Health Record (Department of Health Form CH-14) or its equivalent, updated annually, along with an immunization record , and a special care plan, if applicable
findings.handbook_quote: We also need your child's recent health examination, Universal Child Health Record, immunization record, any special care plan, your signed authorization for emergency medical treatment, and the adults you authorize to pick up your child.

findings.requirement: Upon enrollment, the center must inform parents of its medication and health care procedure policy.
findings.quote: The center shall inform each child’s parent upon enrollment of its policy on administering medication and health care procedures to children
findings.handbook_quote: review our policies on releasing children, toilet training, and giving medication.

findings.requirement: Medication and health care procedures may be administered only after written approval from the parent.
findings.quote: Medication and health care procedures shall be administered only after receipt of written approval from the child's parent(s)
findings.handbook_quote: We give medication and health care procedures only after receiving your written approval, and only designated, trained staff give them.

findings.requirement: The center must take immediate action and notify the parent when specified injuries occur, including bites with broken skin, head or facial injuries, falls from greater than the child's height, or injuries needing professional care.
findings.quote: The center shall take immediate necessary action to protect the child from further harm and shall immediately notify the child's parent(s) when one of the following occurs while the child is in the center’s care
findings.handbook_quote: We call you right away by phone if your child is bitten and the skin is broken, has any head or facial injury (including a bump on the head), falls from higher than their own height, or has an injury that needs professional medical care.

findings.requirement: The center must keep a written record of each specified injury incident with required details.
findings.quote: The center shall maintain on file a written record of each incident resulting in an injury as specified in (a) above
findings.handbook_quote: For other bites and minor injuries, we send a message through our Sparrow Nest parent app and give you a written report at pickup that same day.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not say the center keeps a written record on file for each specified injury with the required details.
findings.fix: We keep a written record on file for every injury that requires immediate notice, including the child's name, date, time, location, description, witnesses, and follow-up care.

findings.requirement: If the center uses a method other than a telephone call for parental notification, it must have a written policy and give it to parents with signed receipts.
findings.quote: The center shall develop and follow a written policy for parental notification if a method other than a telephone call is used at the center for parental notification
findings.handbook_quote: This is our written parental notification policy, and you will sign to confirm you received it.

findings.requirement: The center must develop a written communicable disease policy and give it to parents with signed receipts.
findings.quote: Each center shall develop a written policy on the management of communicable diseases
findings.handbook_quote: This section is our communicable disease policy, and you will sign to confirm you received it.

findings.requirement: A parent or authorized adult must accompany each sick child during admission.
findings.quote: The center shall require that a parent or an adult authorized by the parent accompany each child during admission to the center

findings.requirement: A sick child under three months may not be admitted unless seen and diagnosed by a health care provider who indicates in writing the child can be admitted.
findings.quote: The center shall not admit a sick child below three months of age unless the child has been seen and diagnosed by his or her health care provider who indicates in writing that the child can be admitted

findings.requirement: The center must use a Type I, Type II, or Type S school vehicle for transporting children, except for authorized private passenger vehicles or chartered autobuses under specified conditions.
findings.quote: The center shall use a Type I School Bus, Type II School Bus or Type S School Vehicle at all times when transporting children, except as specified in (f) and (g) below
findings.handbook_quote: Before any field trip, outing, or special event that takes children away from the center by vehicle, we give you written notice at least one week ahead telling you where we are going, whether we will ride a school bus, another approved school vehicle, or a private passenger vehicle, whether the driver is a staff member, a parent, or someone else, and the name and phone number of any bus company.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state that the center uses Type I, Type II, or Type S school vehicles, or authorized private passenger vehicles or chartered autobuses, for transporting children.
findings.fix: When we transport children, we use a Type I, Type II, or Type S school vehicle, or an authorized private passenger vehicle or chartered autobus under the conditions allowed by state rules.

findings.requirement: Children must never be left unattended in a vehicle.
findings.quote: Children shall never be left unattended in a vehicle
findings.handbook_quote: children are never left unattended in a vehicle.

findings.requirement: When one or more children are transported, one adult in addition to the driver must remain in the vehicle while in motion and within sight when stopped to accept or discharge children.
findings.quote: When one or more children are being transported, there shall be one adult in addition to the driver who remains in the vehicle when it is in motion
findings.handbook_quote: at least one adult besides the driver stays with them, and children are never left unattended in a vehicle.

findings.requirement: The center must obtain written authorization from the parent or guardian before transporting a child to or from the center.
findings.quote: The center shall obtain written authorization from the parent or guardian before transporting a child to or from the center
findings.handbook_quote: Your child goes only if you sign a permission slip for that trip.

findings.requirement: Nap-time staffing ratio
findings.quote: A minimum of two staff members, one of whom shall be at least 18 years of age, shall be at the center and involved in the care of children when six or more children are present, except as specified in (l)2 and 3 below.
findings.handbook_quote: nap-time ratios are 1 teacher for 10 children under 18 months, 12 children from 18 months to 2½ years, or 20 children 2½ and older, with a teacher always in the nap room and enough staff in the building to return to awake ratios right away.
findings.explanation: The handbook's one-teacher nap ratios for six or more sleeping children conflict with the rule's minimum of two staff members when six or more children are present.
findings.fix: When six or more children are present, at least two staff members are in the center and involved in their care, including during nap time.

summary: Most handbook statements match the applicable checklist items, with a few partial items and one staffing-ratio conflict. The center should update the partial items and nap-time staffing language to match the rule.
